reader_title: Industrial zoning requires a public zoning review
summary: In Greenfield Township, Fairfield County, the Board of Zoning Appeals decides whether a data center meets the Industrial district’s conditional-use requirements. The amendment took effect July 10, 2026.
locator: §355.04(8); approval and effective dates on p. 2; PDF p. 78
evidence: Data Centers as a Conditional Use

summary: Greenfield measures from a property line next to land zoned or used for homes at the time of application. The board can require more separation based on site conditions. Buildings, generators and parking cannot occupy the setback.
evidence: one thousand (1,000) feet from any property line

thresholds.context: Neighbor zoned or used for housing when the application is filed

reader_title: Connect to central water and sewer
summary: Greenfield Township requires both connections as conditions of the Industrial district’s data center permit.
evidence: all data centers must connect into central water and sewer services

reader_title: Heavy industrial zoning still requires a permit
summary: Metamora treats data centers as advanced manufacturing. The village allows applicants to seek a conditional use permit in the M-3 district, subject to the project standards.
locator: 2026 zoning ordinance, §1427, passed June 1, 2026; PDF p. 67
evidence: may be allowed in the M-3 District as a conditional use

reader_title: Lyons excludes data centers from every zoning district
summary: The village includes data centers in its advanced manufacturing category and bars that use in every district.
locator: Village zoning ordinance, 2026 update, §1430; PDF p. 66
evidence: Advanced Manufacturing uses are not allowed in any zoning district

reader_title: 70 dBA limit at a neighboring property line
summary: Mecklenburg County applies this limit where the neighboring use is not a data center. Exceptions include construction, demolition, emergencies, commissioning, alarms and generator testing during specified hours.

thresholds.context: Boundary shared with a non-data-center use; exceptions in §7.1-8(D)(1)

summary: Use sound-reducing enclosures unless Mecklenburg County’s zoning administrator approves another way to reduce generator noise.
evidence: All generators shall be housed in sound-attenuating enclosures

reader_title: Screen the site from roads and forestland
summary: Mecklenburg requires at least its Type C planted buffer along public roads and specified resource lands, including public parks and commercial timberland. A fence or berm can supplement the planting; changes require zoning approval.

reader_title: Clarksville allows data centers in two districts
summary: The town lists data centers as a permitted use in Business Corridor (B-3) and Tech & Industry (TID). County zoning outside town limits is separate.
locator: Town zoning ordinance, industrial use table, printed p. 052; legend P = permitted as of right; PDF p. 53

reader_title: Three Grayson districts permit data centers
summary: The use table marks data centers as permitted in C-2, C-3 and M-1. Other development approvals may still be needed.
locator: Zoning ordinance revised Feb. 17, 2025, industrial/manufacturing row, §11; legend PDF p. 62; PDF p. 70

reader_title: Orange Township permits data centers in Flex Employment
summary: The Delaware County township marks the FE (Flex Employment) district as permitted in its use table. Other entries on the same row are blank.
locator: Resolution adopted Feb. 3, 2026, Art. 5 use table (printed p. 49); Art. 16 district name; PDF p. 59
